title: California's 36th Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: The general election for California's 36th Congressional District pits six-term Democratic incumbent Ted Lieu against Republican challenger Houston Brignano. The district, a coastal Democratic stronghold stretching from Santa Monica south through Torrance to Rancho Palos Verdes, has a partisan voting index of D+21. Lieu, a member of House Democratic leadership, seeks reelection on a platform of civil rights, immigration reform, and AI regulation, while Brignano, a Marine Corps veteran and technology executive, emphasizes economic opportunity, job training for the AI era, and immigration prioritization for U.S. citizens. The Cook Political Report rates the race as Solid Democratic.
polling_note: No independent opinion polls were found for this general election race. The Cook Political Report rates the district as Solid Democratic.

candidates.name: Ted W. Lieu
candidates.summary: Ted Lieu is a Democrat and the incumbent U.S. Representative for California's 36th Congressional District, first elected in 2014. He serves as Vice Chair of the House Democratic Caucus and sits on the Judiciary and Foreign Affairs Committees. Lieu, a Taiwanese American and naturalized citizen, has a background as an Air Force officer, attorney, and former California state legislator.

candidates.name: Houston Brignano
candidates.summary: Houston Brignano is a Republican candidate and technology executive from the South Bay area of Los Angeles County. A U.S. Marine Corps veteran who served two tours in Iraq, Brignano advocates for AI-focused job training programs, immigration policies that prioritize American workers, and affordable housing solutions. He is running for elected office for the first time.

forecast.rationale: No independent general-election polling is available, limiting confidence from direct voter data. However, strong structural indicators dominate: the district carries a D+21 Partisan Voting Index, is described as a coastal Democratic stronghold, and features a six-term Democratic incumbent (Ted Lieu) who serves in House leadership. The challenger (Houston Brignano) is a first-time candidate in a strongly Democratic district. Cook Political Report rates the race as Solid Democratic. With no evidence of unusual competitiveness from any available source, Democrats maintain an overwhelming advantage.
